clue.text: Ruse failed — sack is certain

indicators.note: a ruse that failed has fallen apart, so its letters come out in a broken order

parts.note: the four letters of ruse rearranged
to sack an employee is to dismiss them

explanation.surface: A trick has gone wrong and someone is now sure to lose their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' reads as the result of the failed ruse, but it simply supplies the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sure-fire is bound to succeed, so the hyphenated adjective is a synonym of certain.

clue.text: Old chestnut? On the contrary

parts.note: surface reading: a stale, much-repeated joke
setter's reading: the opposite of an old chestnut tree, a very young one

explanation.walkthrough: An old chestnut is a hackneyed joke, but read literally it is an aged tree; reverse that and you get a young tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapling is a young tree, the opposite of an ancient chestnut tree.

clue.text: Soldiers will copy sinner

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers
probate is the officially proved copy of a will

explanation.surface: Troops are going to imitate a wrongdoer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like the future tense, but it is a testament, and 'will copy' together give the legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprobate is an unprincipled, immoral person, someone given to wrongdoing.

clue.text: Plant, profuse over most of Thailand once

indicators.note: most of means not quite all, so the old country's name loses its final letter

parts.note: free can mean lavish or generous
Siam was Thailand's former name

explanation.surface: Describing a flower growing abundantly across the former Thai kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Freesia is a fragrant flowering bulb from southern Africa, a garden and florist's plant.

clue.text: Extremely rude, then Samuel expresses regret

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremities of the word, its two ends

parts.note: the first and last letters
Samuel Morse, inventor of the telegraph code

explanation.surface: After being very rude, Samuel says sorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorse is deep regret or guilt for a wrong one has done.

clue.text: At home with wife who's in confinement

parts.note: someone at home is in
a mate is a spouse or partner

explanation.surface: A man at home with his wife, who is shut indoors, perhaps about to give birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confinement' suggests childbirth and the wife, but here it means imprisonment.
explanation.definitionFit: An inmate is a person held in a prison or asylum, so someone kept under lock and key.

clue.text: Being complicated makes it certain to come to grief

indicators.note: coming to grief means meeting with disaster, so the words are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Over-complicating a plan guarantees that it will fail.
explanation.definitionFit: Intricate means very detailed and involved, having many tangled parts, which is complicated.

clue.text: Light going down for second attack

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
an onset is an assault

explanation.surface: As the light fades, the troops launch a fresh assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like 'another', but it means a brief moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonset is the time when the lunar disc sinks below the horizon, a source of light descending.

clue.text: A close call in the field

definitions.text: A close call in the field

parts.note: surface reading: a narrow escape, as in a near miss
setter's reading: a cry given when the quarry is close by, in the hunting field

explanation.walkthrough: 'Close call' means a narrow escape, but here it is a shout raised when the fox is near, and 'the field' is the riders in a hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the huntsman's cry when the fox is sighted, raised by riders following hounds.

clue.text: Sucker may like this name in investment warrant

parts.note: a PEP was a Personal Equity Plan, a British tax-free savings scheme

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for name inside the word for warrant

parts.note: a warrant is an authorising document, a permit
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A fool falling for a financial product, with his name on some certificate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sucker' looks like a dupe drawn to an investment; it is someone sucking a sweet. PEP, a Personal Equity Plan, was a British tax-free savings product of the 1980s and 90s.
explanation.definitionFit: A peppermint is a sweet that is sucked, so it is what a person sucking a sweet would enjoy.

clue.text: Rainwear produced by plant

definitions.meaning: first meaning: short for oilskins, waterproof clothing
second meaning: liquids pressed from seeds such as olive or rape

explanation.surface: Waterproof clothing made in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' suggests a factory, but it is a growing plant that yields vegetable oils.
explanation.definitionFit: Oils is a casual name for oilskin coats, and also the fatty liquids extracted from seeds and fruit.

clue.text: Composer, having gravity, risks no mistakes

indicators.note: mistakes are errors, telling us the preceding words have gone wrong and must be put right in a new order

parts.note: fourteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A serious-minded composer who plays it safe and never errs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian-born writer of The Rite of Spring and The Firebird was a major twentieth-century composer.

clue.text: Classify college leaver not top drawer

indicators.note: not means without, so the class label is taken out of the college leaver

parts.note: someone leaving college with a degree
U means upper-class, the social top drawer

explanation.surface: Ranking students as they leave college, not counting the very best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top drawer' is British slang for the highest social class, and U is the old label for upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To gradate is to arrange in grades or steps, so to sort things into classes by level.

clue.text: Affectionate dispute requiring the judgment of Solomon?

definitions.text: Affectionate dispute requiring the judgment of Solomon?

parts.note: surface reading: a lovers' tiff
setter's reading: Solomon judged two women each claiming the same baby, a custody fight

explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible, Solomon settled two mothers' claims to one child; a modern custody battle carries the same tabloid name.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is British press usage for a custody battle between parents or carers over a child.

clue.text: Dramatised reconstruction made by interested group

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a blend of fact and fiction in film or writing
second meaning: a clique within a party pursuing its own ends

explanation.surface: A docudrama produced by a lobby with a stake in the story.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a fact-based fictional retelling and a dissenting bloc inside a larger organisation.

clue.text: Intervene — at first. I'm on the spot

indicators.note: at first places the short phrase that follows it at the front of the build

parts.note: taken as written
to mediate is to step in between parties

explanation.surface: Someone first steps in to help and announces that they are present at the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Immediate means instant, happening at once, as an on-the-spot decision is made right away.

clue.text: Emphasise the times are normal

parts.note: to aver is to assert firmly
an age is an era or period

explanation.surface: Someone insisting that things these days are perfectly ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Average means typical or ordinary, matching normal as an adjective for the usual run of things.

clue.text: Butcher carves one the guts

indicators.note: to butcher is to hack apart and spoil, so the letters are chopped up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A butcher cutting up a carcass and removing its innards.
explanation.definitionFit: Viscera are the internal organs of the body, especially those of the abdomen, the innards.

clue.text: Toad, say, found route hard to climb

parts.note: a road is a route
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
to climb is to go up, and the word go written upwards in a down entry

explanation.surface: A toad on a hill finding the path a struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Toad in The Wind in the Willows is a reckless motorist. 'Climb' is read as 'go up', which in a down answer is GO written bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A road hog drives selfishly and recklessly, exactly like Kenneth Grahame's motor-mad Toad of Toad Hall.

clue.text: Early bishop repulsed Jew

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: something repulsed is driven back, so the word is turned round

parts.note: a Jew is one of the Semitic peoples

explanation.surface: A bishop early on rejects a Jewish man.
explanation.definitionFit: Betimes is an old adverb meaning in good time or at an early hour.

clue.text: Eliot's Adam holds little boy in manner of doctor

indicators.note: holds means keeps within, so one name sits inside the other

parts.note: Adam Bede is George Eliot's novel and hero
Sid is a short boy's name

explanation.surface: A character from a George Eliot novel holding a small child, as a doctor would.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's way with patients is called a bedside manner, so the word describes the physician's style.

clue.text: Crack regiment, surrounded, lines up missile

indicators.note: the regiment is surrounded, enclosed by the word for crack

parts.note: crack in the sense of first-rate, top
R is an abbreviation for regiment

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: an ode is a poem, lines of verse

explanation.surface: An elite regiment, encircled, deploys a missile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack regiment' reads as one military phrase, but the two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A torpedo is a self-propelled underwater missile fired from a ship or submarine.

clue.text: Flare-up over the lines in a number of flats, maybe

parts.note: to make a scene is to have an angry outburst
RY is the abbreviation for railway, the lines

explanation.surface: An outburst over the railway in a block of apartments.
explanation.walkthrough: Flats look like apartments, but they are painted stage panels; in a down clue 'over' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre flats are painted canvas frames, so several of them make up stage scenery.

clue.text: London stadium where England beat Norway once

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the home ground of Chelsea football club
second meaning: the 1066 battle in Yorkshire where Harold defeated Harald Hardrada

explanation.surface: A football ground where England's team once defeated Norway.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an international football result, but the victory is the battle won by King Harold weeks before Hastings.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to Chelsea's football ground in west London and to a Yorkshire village where a famous battle took place.

clue.text: Letter from abroad for girl from the Marches

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the second letter of the Hebrew alphabet
second meaning: one of the March sisters in Little Women

explanation.surface: A letter posted overseas to a girl living in the Welsh border country.
explanation.walkthrough: The Marches suggests the English-Welsh border region; it is the family in Louisa May Alcott's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Hebrew alphabet character, and the name of the sister who dies young in Alcott's novel.

clue.text: Destroy monastic affiliate for holding perverted rite

indicators.note: perverted means twisted out of its proper form, so the word's letters are rearranged
holding means keeping something within, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: an oblate is a lay person dedicated to a religious order
the letters of rite rearranged

explanation.surface: Wrecking a religious associate for corrupting a ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: To obliterate is to wipe out completely, leaving no trace, which is to destroy utterly.

clue.text: Press hack

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a wringer that squeezes water from laundry
second meaning: to cut roughly, mutilate

explanation.walkthrough: 'Press hack' looks like a journalist, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a roller machine for squeezing washing and a verb for butchering or ruining something.

clue.text: King returns to occupy country at last: the Restoration

indicators.note: something that returns goes back the way it came, so the royal abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: ER is the royal cipher, here for a king
to cover an area is to occupy it

indicators.note: at last points to the very end of the word, keeping only its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of country

explanation.surface: A king comes back to take over the nation: the return of the monarchy in 1660.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to Charles II's return; the definition is a general sense, not the historical period.
explanation.definitionFit: A recovery is a restoring of something lost to its former state, a general sense of restoration.
